title: Sonnets of the Songs-Now the Heart Runs
text:
Now the heart runs over this ground

like impure water before the backwater:

it still carries earth in its dark entrail

and tries to copy the face of heaven.


Pain and longing keep growing,

the current clouds and hurries,

and the sediment of bitterness is more its source

than the wings with which it attempts flight.


If only you stretched out your hand

and the trembling water grew still,

then, gazing long at heaven,


O Desired One!, the heart would let

float upon its transparent dream

the divine beauty of your face.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the heart as muddied water longing to reflect the Desired face.

title: From the Being That Breathes and the Color That Shines
text:
From the being that breathes and the color that shines

your warm presence separates me,

shutting sense inside the vehemence

of a night without bottom and without shore.


In it my tortuous nightmare

confers on you its tragic opulence,

and becomes immortal like an essence,

though you are trivial as clay.


I have begotten you in my flame and my universe;

into your plural form I have projected

the vague complaint and the scattered longing.


The besieged spirit is doubting

whether you are my blood excused in verse

or my pain figured in flesh.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the poem's self-accusation: beloved as projection, blood, verse, and embodied pain.

title: David
text:
O Bathsheba, symbolic and vehement!

With double thirst you wounded my heart

when you made the flame of your body

double itself in the transparent wave.


The rooftop near and the husband absent,

who could resist the bliss of your love?

Not in vain was the image you gave me

a spur to my flanks and to my mind.


Ah me, Bathsheba, your tender arm,

pierced with light like the waves,

bound my flesh to eternal pain!


What horrid blood spattered my boughs!

In what blackness and what terror of winter

was the light of your blond pupils drowned!
editorial_note: The translation keeps David's desire turning into guilt, blood, and winter-darkness.

title: There Is Diluted Moon Beneath Your Eyes...
text:
There is diluted moon beneath your eyes,

and the scent of jasmine, and sad singing;

nostalgia fell asleep in them,

dissolved in the pearls of a sweet weeping...


When you cry, your pure tears sing

the sacred hymns that Eros formed,

and in your arcane dark pupils there are

the deep mysteries Apollo sang.


Dreams faint on their sad satins,

which silently resemble pale sunsets...

pale sunsets of smiling illusion...


While their bonfires light your lips

and the shadows beneath your eyes fasten to your face

the pale blue lily of their heart...




Note: Concha Urquiza wrote this poem when she was 12 years old.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the youthful, ornate imagery and keeps the biographical note.

title: Love, Hidden Current...
text:
Love, hidden current

that moves within the breast,

like a spring that is

feeding my life;

lost in turbid waters,

the sorrowing soul drinks:

if I do not tell it to you, Love,

to whom will I tell my wound?


Flute and laughter, bread and shelter,

let them raise war cries;

the earth brings forth tears

that embitter vine and wheat;

juice of an enemy dart

poisons sweet life:

how shall I weep my sorrow

if I do not weep it with you?


Black wings have stained

the clear summer sky;

the river's breast rears up,

troubled by strong waves:

how shall I cross this ford

if not in your arms, love?

How shall I drink pain

if I do not drink it at your side?
editorial_note: The translation keeps love as hidden current, confidant, crossing, and companion in pain.
